text: Eye-tracked detail levels: a high-res gaze layer plus a low-res layer wider than the eye's range
description:
Render the state at several detail levels driven by the Steam Frame's eye tracking: a fine layer around the gaze and coarse layers further out. The coarse layer covers more than the eye's movement range (and beyond the view edge), so even when the eyes are at one extreme, the opposite side is still rendered (at lower resolution) and never goes stale or empty.

Refined with Felix (2026-11-23):
- Movement always comes from the existing splat reprojection at 90 Hz, for every layer (a head-centred cubemap/360 memory was considered and dropped: zip/swing speeds give too much parallax for a lookup).
- Different net rates per layer: fovea net at 90 Hz, periphery net at ~10 Hz (staggered over tiles, 1/9 per frame).
- Periphery lookahead: the periphery net steps tau = 100 ms ahead (the net already takes tau). The correction (predicted minus reprojected state) is applied 1/9 per frame onto the reprojected state, so content is predicted, not lagging; while computing K(t+200) from K(t+100) in the background.
- Time-stop: just stop advancing the interpolation.
- Fovea and periphery splat into each other; the coarse layers of a learned pyramid (9439aaf2) could be the periphery layers.
- Self-supervised consistency loss: one 100 ms step ~ nine 11 ms steps (no real data needed).
- The net keeps learning to fill edge/corner holes (Felix: rely on the net there).

status.comment: Groundwork: eye gaze is read (XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction), u.gaze per eye in all shaders; the focus fader uses it. 2026-11-23: train.semigroup loss added (one step of tau vs two of tau/2, no truth). Measured on nice-net, random state, tau = 2.4 (100 ms at rate 24): the semigroup gap is 0.0014 vs a mean rgb step of 0.029 (~5%), so a 100 ms periphery step is already roughly consistent with small steps; the loss is a safeguard, not urgent. Multi-resolution layers in the app not started.
